implementation: The publishable opencode-dispatch-plugin@0.1.0 package exposes only ./server and ./tui, embeds prebuilt PWA assets, declares MIT and engines.opencode >=1.18.3 <2, and has no main, postinstall, workspace runtime dependency, or source map.

A deterministic pack harness performs two clean builds, proves byte-identical tarball hashes, enforces an explicit path and size allowlist, scans the actual extracted archive for credentials, local paths, and source maps, verifies direct dependency licenses, and installs without lifecycle scripts.

The isolated OpenCode fixture installs the exact generated tarball through a disposable loopback npm registry into OpenCode's disposable package cache, then uses the official global plugin command for server/TUI target detection and JSONC mutation while proving live user config hashes remain unchanged.
Broker configuration now carries an explicit validated port through election, HTTP, and WebSocket paths; a live overridden-port test proves a foreign listener is diagnosed and left serving.

Packed server and TUI target functions launch from the disposable installation: the server answers cluster health on an isolated overridden port with disposable state, and the TUI registers then disposes its command without optional OpenTUI peers.
Unsupported OpenCode 1.18.2 and 2.0.0 fixture selections emit an actionable range warning and skip every activation case before artifact creation or config mutation.

The native CI workflow covers macOS 14, Ubuntu 24.04, and Windows 2025 with OpenCode 1.18.3 and current latest 1.18.25, Bun 1.3.14, pinned actions, frozen installs, package verification, typecheck, and Biome.

red.observed: OpenCode 1.18.x accepts an absolute tarball argument but resolves its manifest beside the archive and exits with Manifest read failed instead of loading package/package.json.
red.resolution: The fixture exposes the exact generated archive through a temporary local registry, installs that archive into the isolated OpenCode cache with scripts disabled, and then runs the official global target command against the exact package version. No workspace source or live config participates.

red.observed: The initial current-latest fixture was pinned to 1.18.21 after npm had advanced.
red.resolution: npm view opencode-ai version returned 1.18.25; the local fixture default and six-job matrix now pin 1.18.25.

red.observed: A malformed-JSONC failure-path test exceeded Bun's default five-second test timeout after the real isolated install was added.
red.resolution: Package setup and integration cases now have explicit 120-second bounds and pass while proving both config files and live hashes remain unchanged.

red.observed: Post-implementation review found incomplete registry cleanup, Unix-only live-config hashing, no packed target launch, and no deterministic unsupported-version skip.
red.resolution: The full registry lifetime now uses finally cleanup, subprocesses are bounded, config hashing follows Windows APPDATA or Unix XDG paths, packed targets launch from the installed artifact, and below-minimum/2.x fixtures warn then skip before mutation.

red.observed: Fresh code-quality review found registry shutdown was initiated but not awaited and command timeouts killed only the direct child process.
red.resolution: Registry shutdown is now awaited; POSIX commands run in a detached process group killed as a unit, while Windows uses taskkill /t /f. Timeout diagnostics are explicit, robots.txt joins extracted text scanning, and strict version parsing rejects leading-zero or malformed values.
